title: Input case sensitivity attribute

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
Hi,

## The need
Some `input` fields on the web are case-sensitive like passwords, usernames or sometimes URL and host names. Therefore, Opquast blog (Web quality) says that "A website must show a hint to user if the case lock in activated when inserted text in a case-sensitive field". IMO, this is an interesting idea to show the user a hint when a field is case-sensitive, but this should be set at the spec level of HTML instead of being implemented by every website in their own way.

### The showcases
* Password are usually case-sensitive (should this behaviour be a default one, like all `type="password"` fields are marked as case-sensitive by default?)
* Username
* Email address
* URL (their parameters can be case sensitive)
* Any field that will then be used in hashing (hash functions works on byte level, so they are case sensitive)
* Search forms (case sensitivity can usually be toggled in such forms)


### Draft proposal
So having a standard way to tell that an `input` is case-sensitive will bring a better user experience.
To do so, an `input` field could have a new boolean attribute `casesensitivity` telling that this field is case-sensitive. Therefore, the conforming UA should show user a warning if the input device is in upper or lower case lock.

But I see the two possible issues with this: 
* The attribute name `casesensitivity` may be a bit odd to write (ca-se-se-ntivity).
* The attribute is not extensible. 

## Proposal
A more abstracted version should be preferred, allowing to tell about case sensitivity, but also about accents (will the server consider `a == à` for this input?) or localization issues (will the server interprete thousand separators?) An attribute like `sensitivity` that is a set of space-separated tokens (`case`, `accent`, `thousand-separator`...) would allow a lot of possible extensions later (even vendor-defined ones like `-moz-...`?)

So I suggest to discuss about such `sensititivy` attribute to improve user experience when filling a form field. If required, I might dig a bit to see what UAs implementors (Firefox/Chrome/Opera/Edge) think about such thing.
